sovereign_country.strategic_role: 亚太高客单价数字内容、游戏出海与本土电商合规

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Open-Market Brokerage of Solid-State Drives and Server Processors

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Protection of Investments
Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America
Convention between the Republic of Korea and the Republic of France for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: South Korea's AML/CFT legal framework is principally the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as last amended, often called the Financial Transaction Reports Act), its Presidential Enforcement Decree, and the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. The Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the Financial Services Commission enforces customer due diligence, requiring obliged financial companies to collect and verify the beneficial owner of each legal-person customer. The Commercial Act and the Registration of Commerce Act govern Chusik Hoesa formation and the corporate shareholder register; the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act governs foreign investment and cross-border payments. No public UBO register exists; beneficial owner data is held internally by the obliged institution and made available to government AML/CFT supervisors on lawful demand.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Registered Matters)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court Registry Office of the local district court having jurisdiction, Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean-registry certification, then either Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea when the receiving jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state, or Consular Legalization by the Korean diplomatic mission with consular authority over the receiving state when it is not. The two routes are mutually exclusive alternatives and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Clearance Certificate / Certified Statement of Complete Payment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea via the local District Tax Office or Regional Tax Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: National Tax Service issuance, then either Hague Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention recipients, or Consular Legalization by the Korean consulate for non-members. No sequential combination of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Foreign Incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the ultimate beneficial owner or parent entity, notarized by a licensed notary in the document's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If origin country is an Apostille Convention state: local notarization, then Apostille by that state's competent authority, followed by certified Korean translation. If origin country is a non-member: local notarization, then legalization by the Korean consulate or foreign ministry per the local legalization procedure. The two actions are mutually exclusive and cannot be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding incorporators and a notary public under the Korean Notary Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean notarization, then Hague Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Hague-member destination, or Consular Legalization by the appropriate Korean consulate for non-Hague destination. Select only one path as applicable; never layer both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Beneficial Owner and Prospective Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution of the UBO or parent company, signed by a senior banking officer and notarized as required in the source jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: bank letter notarized and Apostilled by the source-state competent authority; for non-Apostille states: notarized and legalized through the Republic of Korea's diplomatic or consular representation. The legalization routes are parallel alternatives, never sequential.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All identified UBOs, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and counterparties must be screened pre-filing and on a continuous 24-hour rolling basis. Mandatory screening libraries include the UN Security Council Consolidated List, US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Non-SDN Consolidated Lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions, Interpol notices, Korean FIU watchlists and sanction notices under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. PEP classification must cover foreign and domestic prominent public functions, immediate family, close associates, and known legal entities controlled by a PEP. Any hit requires rejection or risk-mitigated enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, and a suspicious transaction report to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit within the statutory deadline. Enhanced due diligence must be documented for the medium-risk semiconductor broker scope and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Republic of Korea Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (iREG) - Commercial Registration Search / Trade Name Search System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal registered name of a Chusik Hoesa must be stated in Korean (Hangul), and where the name contains a foreign word, it must be written in accepted Korean transliteration; auxiliary Latin characters or numerals may be used, but the registered trade name is the Hangul version. Korean registry practice follows a four-tier naming scheme: (1) territorial or regional chip, (2) distinctive trade-name element, (3) industry or object-clause descriptor, and (4) legal-form suffix 'Chusik Hoesa'. The trade name must not be deceptively identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered trade name conducting similar business within the same registry district and Korea-wide protected scope.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the iREG name clearance is rejected, the applicant must promptly download the registry officer's stated rejection reason and, within 30 calendar days, file a formal written objection and request for reconsideration with the head of the competent registration office. The objection must include the rejected name, the registry citation or reference number, a corrected name if any, a legal basis for registrability, and evidence of non-conflicting use. If the registry denies reconsideration, the applicant may, through Korean counsel, file an appeal under the Registration of Commerce Act or the Administrative Litigations Act depending on the act complained of. Where an initial reservation is nearing expiry, a written extension request should be filed before expiration, attaching evidence of notarization in progress, and the registry may grant an additional 30 days upon good cause. During any appeal, the applicant should also file parallel alternative names to avoid project delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The Korean registry will honor a virtual office or registered address only if it is a physical street address and a designated resident agent can receive legal notices on site. Nonetheless, the National Tax Service and domestic banking counterparties will, for a wholesale SSD and CPU chip broker classified as ISIC 4651 and AML medium-risk enhanced, reject a pure virtual-office or mail-box arrangement. The company must maintain a physical business office with lease in the corporate name, employee presence, record storage, telecommunications, and verifiable trade documentation. A serviced office or executive suite may be acceptable if it has actual counters, signage, and staff; a mere commercial mailbox is non-compliant for tax invoice issuance, VAT registration, and corporate account opening.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sang-beop), Act No. 1000, as currently consolidated; stock-corporation formation is governed by Articles 288 through 318, including Article 289 (notarized articles of incorporation), Article 295 (payment for issued shares), Article 296 (defects in shares), Article 300 (election of directors and auditor), Article 312 (auditor), and Article 317 (registration of incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the company's registered principal office; electronic filing through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (iROs) portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa filed under the Commercial Act with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and the certified paid-in capital deposit certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Chusik Hoesa. All subscribed shares must be fully paid before registration, and the paid-in capital must be deposited in a domestic Korean bank in the Company's name or in a subscription-custody account. The bank issues the paid-in capital certificate required for registration. No formal blocked escrow-account rule exists under the Commercial Act; however, foreign investors must comply with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and maintain inbound telegraphic-transfer or foreign-exchange purchase records for the paid-in capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. The Board of Directors (the "Board") held its first meeting on [DATE] at the Company's registered office in [CITY], Republic of Korea. The Chairman having certified that a quorum of directors was present in person or by videoconference permitted under the Articles of Incorporation, the Board adopted the following formal resolutions. 1. RATIFICATION OF CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND SHARE ISSUANCE. RESOLVED, that the subscriptions for and issuance of [NUMBER] ordinary shares, with a par value of KRW [AMOUNT] per share, fully paid into the Company's capital deposit account in accordance with Article 295 of the Commercial Act, be and hereby are ratified and confirmed. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chief Financial Officer is directed to maintain the shareholder ledger and to issue share certificates to each registered shareholder in accordance with Article 349 of the Commercial Act. 2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE AND CORPORATE SEAL. RESOLVED, that the registered office and statutory seat of the Company be and remain at [ADDRESS], Republic of Korea; the corporate seal and bank seal are approved as submitted; and the President is authorized to register the seal with the court registry, tax office, banks, and counterparties and to affix the seal to all corporate instruments. 3. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that [NAME] be appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, that [NAME] be appointed Chief Financial Officer, and that [NAME] be appointed Auditor, each for a term and compensation specified in the Articles of Incorporation and the Board's compensation schedule, and that such officers be vested with the duties, authorities, and restrictions imposed by the Commercial Act and corporate policy. 4. BANKING AND PAYMENT RAILS AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the opening of all bank accounts, including SWIFT Telegraphic Transfer accounts and Escrow-Inspection Wire accounts, at [BANK] is authorized; any two authorized signatories among the President, the Chief Financial Officer, and the Compliance Officer shall affix their signatures or corporate seal in accordance with the banking mandate cards. 5. COMPLIANCE AND DELEGATION. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to apply for tax registration, to submit all filings to the tax authority, to engage in any lawful foreign-exchange transaction, and to retain legal counsel for export-control and trade-compliance matters. RESOLVED, that management shall adopt and implement anti-money-laundering and beneficial-ownership verification procedures consistent with Korean financial regulations. This resolution and all actions taken pursuant to it are hereby approved, adopted and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation, Capital Subscription, and Officer Consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public under the Notary Act, assisted by a licensed judicial scrivener; notarial office of the city where the articles are drafted
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder must prepare Korean-language articles of incorporation that include the company name, business purpose, address of registered office, number of authorized shares, par value, share classes, public notice method, and auditor provisions. Each business purpose must be drafted to cover wholesale brokerage of solid-state drives and server processors under ISIC 4651. The articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public, who will verify the identity and authority of all founders or their lawful agents. Landlord consent or a lease contract confirming use of the registered-office address must be presented. The founders must sign the share subscription list and confirm that each director and auditor candidate consents to appointment. If any correction is required, the notary may require a revised draft and re-authentication.
required_dossiers: Completed draft Articles of Incorporation
Founders' valid passports or alien registration cards
Power of attorney appointing the Korean agent or judicial scrivener
Lease agreement or landlord consent for the registered office
Share subscription statements signed by founders
Written consents of proposed directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication due to missing address, consent, or representative authority, obtain the corrected lease, consent form, or corporate authorization and resubmit the full notarization package within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-In Capital and Issuance of the Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank in the Republic of Korea authorized under the Commercial Act and licensed by the Financial Supervisory Service for foreign-exchange business
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, all subscribed share consideration must be remitted to a domestic Korean bank in accordance with Article 295 of the Commercial Act. The bank will open a subscription-deposit record or issue a capital deposit certificate confirming that the required funds are in custody for the company. The funds may not be withdrawn before incorporation registration. For foreign investors, the inbound telegraphic transfer must be reported or otherwise performed through an authorized foreign-exchange bank, and source-of-funds documentation must be preserved. The bank will issue a certificate, ledger entry, or receipt that the incorporation registration court will require. The company should verify that the certificate names the company and matches the total subscribed capital in the articles.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital subscription list and allotment record
Foreign-exchange purchase or inbound remittance record
Identification documents of subscribers or beneficial owners
Bank account application and anti-money-laundering declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, the applicant must submit the full inbound wire record, sender declaration, and beneficial-ownership statement; the deposit certificate can then be re-issued within the same business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Incorporation Registration at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office; iROs electronic filing portal of the Supreme Court of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following issuance of the capital deposit certificate, the founder or licensed judicial scrivener must file the incorporation registration application with the competent court registry. The filing may be submitted electronically through iROs or in paper form at the registry counter. The court will verify the notarized articles, the capital deposit certificate, the appointment of directors and auditor, the corporate seal registration, and the registered-office evidence. Once the court is satisfied, it enters the company into the commercial register, assigns the corporate registration number, and issues a certified corporate registration extract. Under Article 317, the company comes into existence on the date and time of such registration. Any defect in the articles or attachments must be cured before registration.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate or ledger confirmation
Written consent and appointment evidence for directors and auditor
Certified copy of the share subscription record
Power of attorney for the submitting scrivener or agent
Corporate seal card application and specimen
Government filing fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a query or correction order, the applicant must cure the identified defect within the statutory correction period, typically the time specified in the order; if the registration lapses, a corrected filing with a new application and receipt must be submitted promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea; local district tax office with jurisdiction over the company's head office; electronic filing through Hometax
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: A newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa must file for business registration before carrying on business or within twenty days after incorporation, whichever is earlier. The taxpayer representative or tax agent must submit the electronic application through Hometax, indicating the company name, head-office address, representative, business type, and place of business. The business type should be described as wholesale trade of computer storage devices, semiconductor processors, and related electronic equipment. The tax office will verify the certified corporate register extract, lease or address evidence, corporate seal, and officer identity. After approval, the National Tax Service issues a business registration certificate with a ten-digit tax identification number, registers the company for value-added tax and corporate tax, and activates the electronic tax-invoice system.
required_dossiers: Certified corporate register extract issued after incorporation
Notarized or certified Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement or landlord consent for the head office
Corporate seal certificate or seal card specimen
Representative's passport or Korean residence certificate
Business registration application form
Power of attorney if using a tax agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service suspends the application because of an address or representative discrepancy, file corrected lease evidence, updated official register extract, or corrected identity documentation; an appeal or correction request may be filed within thirty days if the suspension is not resolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening the First Board of Directors Meeting and Post-Registration Banking Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Directors; Financial Supervisory Service-licensed Korean commercial bank; company officers authorized under the first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after incorporation registration and tax registration, the directors must convene the first board meeting to adopt the formal first-board resolutions set out in this dossier. The minutes must be signed by the attending directors and ratified. The approved resolutions are then used to complete corporate banking onboarding. The bank must conduct customer due diligence, identify the beneficial owners, verify officers, and establish the corporate signatory authority. The Company will submit the board resolution, certified register extract, business registration certificate, corporate seal card, and personal identification of all signatories. The bank will activate SWIFT telegraphic-transfer and escrow-inspection wire payment rails, and the company will maintain transaction and contract records required for its medium-risk enhanced anti-money-laundering classification.
required_dossiers: First Board of Directors resolution and execution copy
Certified corporate register extract and seal certificate
Business registration certificate
Board-approved banking mandate and signatory list
Passports or residence tax numbers of all signatories
Beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds declarations
Escrow and foreign-exchange instruction forms if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays onboarding because of anti-money-laundering concerns, the company must furnish additional beneficial-owner declarations and remittance provenance; if the board quorum is challenged, convene a corrected meeting and ratify the minutes by unanimous written consent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. ISIC 4651 wholesale trade of solid-state drives and server processors is not a manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity falling within ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx, so no industrial licensing board is engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. The only operational prerequisite is the business registration certificate issued by the National Tax Service for wholesale-trade activity; no separate industrial operating permit is required for spot semiconductor trading.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. Ministry of Environment and its EIA administration are not triggered for wholesale brokerage without manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehousing operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. The proposed activity is pure wholesale trading and therefore does not require a full Environmental Impact Assessment, Strategic Environmental Assessment, or environmental site registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. No process wastewater, volatile organic compound emission, or hazardous-waste discharge arises from ISIC 4651 wholesale trading. If the company later operates a physical distribution warehouse, the applicable thresholds under the Clean Air Conservation Act, Water Environment Conservation Act, and Wastes Control Act must be reviewed at that time.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for office-based wholesale operations; no Civil Defense fire-safety permit is required for a non-manufacturing, non-warehousing trading office. If the company later establishes a physical warehouse or industrial installation, the National Fire Agency and local fire department must verify the fire-safety installation certificate and emergency-evacuation compliance, and the Ministry of Employment and Labor would require occupational-safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; official electronic portal: HomeTax (Hometax) at https://www.hometax.go.kr. Korea Customs Service (KCS) operates the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system for export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that establishes a Korean place of business, permanent establishment, or VAT-registerable supply activity must apply for a Business Registration Certificate (business registration number) from the district tax office with jurisdiction over the Korean place of business. On approval, the 10-digit Business Registration Number serves concurrently as the Corporate Tax TIN and the VAT ID. The registration application may be submitted in person by the foreign corporation's local tax representative or certified tax accountant, or electronically through the NTS HomeTax portal using the corporation's digital certificate. Required evidentiary documents generally include: home-country articles of incorporation and certificate of incorporation/good standing (apostilled or legalized as required), board resolution appointing a Korean tax/agent representative, power of attorney, passport/ID copies of the signing local representative, evidence of the Korean business premises (lease agreement or ownership certificate), and, if a branch is registered, the Korean court-stamped branch registration certificate. The same registration is used for VAT, corporate income tax, and withholding obligations; the taxpayer must obtain a tax representative for service of process under the Framework Act on National Taxes if no Korean resident is appointed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily treated as a domestic corporation under the Korean Corporate Income Tax Act; no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch classification election is available. Qualifying wholly owned Korean group companies may elect group consolidation filing for corporate income tax purposes, but that election does not alter the entity-level tax classification or VAT separation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Korean Value-Added Tax (under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 - compulsory VAT registration on commencement of business; the Korean VAT Act does not provide a general monetary exemption threshold for VAT registration. A simplified taxable-person filing regime exists for certain small individual entrepreneurs whose prior-year annual taxable supplies do not exceed KRW 80,000,000, but this does not eliminate the registration requirement or apply to a stock corporation acting as a wholesale exporter.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-invoice) system through the NTS HomeTax platform. All VAT-registered businesses that issue tax invoices are required to issue, transmit, and store e-invoices electronically through HomeTax, an authorized e-document service provider, or an ERP integration using NTS-approved APIs; paper tax invoices remain only in permitted exceptional circumstances. There is no pre-clearance or real-time fiscal stamping regime like those used in certain other jurisdictions. Anti-fraud controls rely on unique e-invoice numbers, digital certification, cross-matching of e-invoices with VAT returns and customs export records, and prescribed statutory transmission deadlines (generally aligned with quarterly VAT return periods).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT zero-rating applies under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act to goods actually exported from Korea. The statutory conditions require: (1) the seller is a VAT-registered Korean exporter; (2) the goods are sold to a foreign non-resident buyer or foreign purchaser; (3) an export declaration is lodged and accepted through Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS); (4) the goods are physically shipped outside the Korean customs territory; (5) a zero-rated tax invoice is issued to the foreign buyer; and (6) the export proceeds are collected through a permitted foreign exchange transaction and the payment evidence is retained. The sale must be an arm's-length commercial sale, and the exporter must preserve sufficient customs and foreign-exchange records to substantiate the physical export and value. Qualifying offshore services supplied to non-residents may also be zero-rated where consumed outside Korea and paid in foreign currency; however, under the ISIC 4651 wholesale of SSD and CPU chips, goods exports are the controlling transaction type.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Cargo Clearance Certificate issued by Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS export declaration acceptance record)
Original or electronic Bill of Lading for ocean shipments or Master Air Waybill for air shipments
Bank-issued Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate / Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Export sales contract or purchase order
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) issued to the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service use the export declaration and bank foreign-exchange receipt records as the primary audit trail for export zero-rating. If the exporter fails to produce the mandatory documentation bundle, or if the export is shown to be fictitious, the proceeds are not received within the prescribed repatriation term (generally 180 days from export clearance unless a bank-approved extension is obtained), or the payment is received through a non-qualifying channel, the 0% VAT rate is retroactively disallowed. NTS will assess the unpaid VAT at 10%, add statutory additional tax for late/improper filing, impose interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and may reassess corporate income tax on the unreported foreign-exchange income. Refunds already paid to the exporter are clawed back with the statutory extra tax and interest. For fraudulent documentation, criminal sanctions are available under the Value-Added Tax Act and related customs and foreign-exchange statutes, and the statutory assessment limitation period extends to ten years for fraudulent or undisclosed transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act of the Republic of Korea
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea operates a liberalised but administratively supervised foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations. Current-account payments, including trade settlements, service charges, and remittances of distributable profits, are generally free of quantitative restriction; settlement must be routed through a registered foreign exchange bank or licensed foreign financial institution. Capital-account transactions, notably inward direct investment, acquisition of equity, loans, and external debt, remain subject to a post-acceptance risk management framework: an investor or domestic company must file a foreign-exchange declaration or obtain prior approval, depending on the transaction, and transfers against the resulting foreign-currency holding must preserve its traceable nature through the Korea Foreign Exchange Information System. Export proceeds need not be converted into KRW unless the exporter uses a domestic account; however, the export receipt must be realised within the statutory collection period under the relevant export report, and any discrepancy between invoice value and credited amount triggers an adverse-information review. Profit repatriation by a Korean entity requires a valid settlement certificate, audited distributable profits, and proof of payment of corporate income tax, plus a bank confirmation that the dividend distribution was duly filed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. In practice, banks act as gatekeepers, demanding underlying contracts, customs declarations, and shareholder resolutions before executing dividend or capital-account wires. Cross-border KRW clearing is available through domestic foreign exchange banks and the BOK-Wire+ system, but non-resident KRW accounts are subject to use restrictions, and synthetic offshore KRW products are not treated as permitted settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds for ordinary shipments of SSD/CPU goods must be received within 18 months from the date of the export declaration, unless the exporter obtains an extension from the designated foreign exchange bank before the deadline. There is no statutory percentage surrender requirement; the exporter may keep the full 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency, but the receipt must be recorded through a registered foreign exchange bank and driven into the Korea Foreign Exchange Information System. Any amount exceeding the invoice or retained beyond the deadline without extension is regarded as an unrecovered export reported item and may block future bank settlements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Banking Act restrict the execution of foreign exchange business and cross-border payment settlement to banks licensed by the MOEF and to registrants expressly permitted to conduct foreign exchange operations. Domestic simple payment institutions and offshore EMIs such as digital-only money transmitters cannot lawfully open KRW corporate operating accounts, perform export-proceeds surrender, or issue capital verification certificates for a Chusik Hoesa. Offshore EMIs are therefore viable only as invoicing or e-commerce payment acceptance tools in the counterparty's jurisdiction; they must never be used as the Korean treasury or settlement rail because their incoming transfers do not satisfy Korean customs, capital verification, and VAT export evidence rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical in-branch appearance is required for the statutory director and the beneficial owner, or for a person with valid board-approved power of attorney, at the account-holding branch. Korean banks do not permit remote consular proxy opening for a domestic limited company; the opening signatory must appear before a branch compliance officer, present original board resolution, corporate seal registration certificate, passport and alien registration card, UBO declaration, and supporting business contracts. For a foreign-only board, at least one authorised financial officer must attend the interview and the bank may require an additional interview with a local resident accountable officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate beneficial ownership chain with a foreign Chusik Hoesa shareholder and no Korean-based UBO on the register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the shareholder registry, complete group-structure chart, UBO declaration under the Commercial Act and Act on Corporate Governance of Financial Companies, individual tax identification certificates for each 10%+ shareholder, notarized passport copies, and board resolution confirming UBO transfer restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use or strategically controlled semiconductor merchandise triggers suspicion in the bank's trade sanctions screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ECCN/HTS classification memorandum for SSDs and server CPUs, Korea Strategic Trade Institute (KOSTI) automated screening opinion, supplier and buyer end-user certificates, denial-list screening output, and full purchase orders and customs export declarations showing physical movement and third-party logistics details.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags due to price volatility on spot semiconductor trades, advance payments, and settlements not aligned with the SSD/CPU delivery cycle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master trading agreement, pro forma invoice and all contract exhibits, bank-internal settlement instruction for each transaction not exceeding product-specific trading tolerances, original bills of lading or airway bills, bonded warehouse entry receipts, third-party escrow inspection certificate, marine/air cargo insurance policy, and a written golden-rule explanation for any settlement adjustment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign statutory director's identity or authority cannot be independently verified without a physical alien registration card and apostilled legalisation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution delegating account opening power, apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney, passport bio page with immigration arrival stamp, alien registration card, lease contract for the Korean registered office, and an in-branch compliance interview transcript verified by the bank's CCTV record.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward equity capital injection for the Korean Chusik Hoesa must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank to the beneficiary KRW/foreign currency settlement account at a Korea foreign exchange bank. The remitting bank must state the purpose code for inward direct investment under the Foreign Exchange Information System transaction classification table, and the Korean entity must file the foreign-exchange declaration with the receiving bank either pre-transaction or within the statutory grace period for non-trade capital receipts. The bank will allocate the incoming funds to a capital contribution ledger and issue a settlement certificate; an independent Korean certified public accountant must then verify the receipt, board resolution, share issuance details, and paid-in capital requirement to complete the statutory capital verification report for the registry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments for wholesale SSD and CPU purchases should primarily settle through SWIFT MT103 for open-account transactions in USD or KRW where the commercial invoice is verified against the import declaration and the exporter's banking instructions. For first-time or high-value counterparty exposure, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) opened by the Korean bank and advised through the seller's confirming bank offers protection; Documentary Collections (DP/DA) are less recommended because document mismatch disputes can leave settlement stranded. Each disbursement must reference the underlying contract and customs identifier so the bank can map the payment to the beneficiary's export transaction and maintain a clean audit trail for the MOEF reporting system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD-KRW forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, limited to the firm's documented underlying import/export exposure.
KRW/USD cross-currency swaps for long-term trade-related financing or non-resident receivables, subject to exchange bank limits and the establishment of eligible underlying debt.
FX options (European-style) with a licensed bank for hedging forecast trade cash flows where premium and strike are determined in the onshore KRW market.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) hedges are narrowly permitted only for entities with genuine trade exposure and are blocked for speculative or purely financial postures; offshore synthetic KRW products are not permissible settlement substitutes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment (Korean Chusik Hoesa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea (NTS) via HomeTax local district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underreporting negligence penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax (or 40% for fraudulent understatement), plus daily delinquency surcharge of 0.022%-0.03% on overdue tax; chronic non-filing can lead to enforced tax collection, seizure of bank accounts and assets, cancellation of the business registration, and judicial dissolution of a dormant company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Surtax Return and Payment (Local Income Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent municipal Si-Gun-Gu local tax authority (delegated collection through the National Tax Service)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as national corporate income tax; for a December 31 fiscal year, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax non-filing and non-payment trigger penalties of up to 20% of the understated local income tax amount plus delinquency interest at the statutory daily rate; persistent failure results in administrative collection and registration cancellation measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' General Meeting and Approval of Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing authority for the meeting itself; meeting minutes and resolutions are retained at the registered office and bylaw-relevant court registration matters are filed with the competent Korean Registry Court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of each fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the statutory annual meeting within the deadline are subject to indemnification liability and punitive fines under the Korean Commercial Act; repeated failure or dormant-company status for 5 years may trigger court-adjudicated dissolution and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report Submission (for Mandatorily Audited Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service of Korea (FSS) through DART electronic disclosure, with audit report copy transmission to the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit opinion must be ready for the annual shareholders' meeting; for a December 31 fiscal year, by March 31; disclosure to FSS/DART is required within the period prescribed by the External Audit Act after report issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or non-compliant audit reports expose the auditor and the company to administrative fines up to KRW 50 million, imprisonment not exceeding 1 year, or both; misuse of unqualified/unapproved financial statements is treated as a serious corporate governance violation and can be referred to the Korean Board of Audit and Inspection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Return and Annual Aggregate Tax Invoice List (for Wholesale Chip Trading)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea (VAT return through HomeTax electronic filing system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second-half VAT final return for a January-December fiscal year is due by January 25 of the following year; the annual aggregate tax invoice list is due by February 10 of the following year; the first-half preliminary return is due by July 25 of the current year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the aggregate invoice list and VAT return results in additional tax of 1%-2% of invoice value or output VAT omitted, late-filing surcharges, and daily delinquency interest on unpaid VAT; severe non-compliance can suspend the VAT business registration and trigger criminal tax charges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Status Report and 30-Day Material Change Report (if Foreign-Invested Joint-Stock Company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) of Korea, delegated to KOTRA and designated foreign-exchange banks
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual foreign-investment status confirmation due on the anniversary of the foreign investment registration, or by the Korean regulatory deadline for a December fiscal year; any 10% or greater shareholding transfer, ownership ratio change, or statutory foreign-investment classification change must be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file foreign-investment annual or change reports may result in administrative fines, loss of foreign-investment protection under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, delayed dividend remittance recognition, and adverse handling by Korean customs and foreign-exchange authorities for cross-border SSD and CPU purchase settlements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Chusik Hoesa must be independently audited by a licensed Korean CPA firm if any of the following applies: (i) total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million at 1,300 KRW/USD); (ii) the company is a listed company or publicly offers securities; (iii) the company is a financial institution or otherwise designated by the Financial Services Commission as requiring external audit; or (iv) special statutes impose an audit requirement. For ordinary unlisted private wholesalers of SSD/CPU chips, the objective statutory trigger is the KRW 12 billion balance-sheet test; there is no separate turnover or employee-count audit trigger for such an entity. Non-audited smaller companies may nevertheless voluntarily obtain a certified audit for banking, escrow, or counterparty due diligence purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Mandatory audited companies must prepare financial statements under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), consistent with IFRS as adopted in Korea; private non-listed companies without a statutory audit may apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) or the Korean SME Accounting Standards. The audit itself is performed in accordance with Korean Auditing Standards (KSA), aligned with International Standards on Auditing (ISA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not maintain a general one-size-fits-all annual UBO declaration for a private Chusik Hoesa. Beneficial ownership is instead confirmed through mandatory mechanisms: (i) every share transfer must be recorded in the shareholders register kept at the registered office, so the register is continuously updated rather than annually submitted; (ii) a 30-day material change report to KOTRA/MOTIE is required for any foreign investor acquiring, disposing of, or altering a 10% or greater non-resident shareholding; (iii) banking and AML rules under the Financial Intelligence Unit of Korea require the company to provide current beneficial-owner information to its Korean bank and to update it upon KYC periodic review, usually on an annual review cycle; and (iv) if the company is foreign-invested, the annual foreign-investment status report to KOTRA serves as the formal annual confirmation protocol. For a spot-semiconductor wholesale company engaged in cross-border wire transfers, the bank's enhanced due diligence will require an annual beneficial-ownership attestation even if no regulatory UBO registry form exists.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registered Charges, Pledges and Share Transfer Endorsement Records
Minutes Book of General Meetings of Shareholders
Minutes Book of Board of Directors Meetings
Articles of Incorporation and Corporate Seal Register
Directors and Statutory Auditor Appointment Record

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - USD 700 per annum for registered office or licensed corporate agent address service; USD 300 - USD 800 per annum additional for professional corporate secretarial handling of annual filings, minute books, court registry updates, and NTS/KOTRA compliance coordination.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 18,000 per annum for a certified CPA audit by a Korean licensed firm for an unlisted, cross-border wholesale semiconductor trading entity depending on transaction volume, number of escrow wires, inventory turnover, and transfer-pricing complexity; USD 0 if the entity remains below the mandatory audit threshold and no voluntary audit is contracted.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive rates: 10% on first KRW 200 million; 20% on the next bracket up to KRW 20 billion; 22% up to KRW 300 billion; 25% above KRW 300 billion. Additional incentives under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (e.g., R&D tax credits up to 25% of qualifying expenditure, job-creating investment tax credits, SME reduced rates of 10% for income ≤KRW 200 million, and tax holidays for free economic zone foreign investors).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return on Net Income (법인세과세표준및세액신고서) - Form No. 15 / electronic filing via the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with semi-annual preliminary corporate tax payments in August and October for fiscal-year taxpayers)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by March 31 for a December 31 year-end). Foreign corporations may apply for a one-month extension under Article 98 of the Corporate Income Tax Act; further extension possible for Korean-party transactions reviewed by foreign tax authorities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total domestic and international sales revenue from wholesale trading of SSD and CPU chips, including brokerage commissions if acting as agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all sales gross, without netting procurement costs. Foreign-source sales to non-Korean customers may be excluded if attributable to a foreign permanent establishment and properly documented. Cross-border sales through e-commerce platforms must be recognized on delivery dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of semiconductor inventory sold, including purchase price, freight, customs duties and import charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For related-party purchases, apply arm's-length pricing and maintain TP documentation. Imported goods from related suppliers must be supported by CIF invoices. Inventory valuations must be in KRW at the exchange rate on the date of acquisition.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: rent, salaries, advertising, professional fees, depreciation, insurance, and head office allocations (for foreign corporations).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign head office general and administrative expenses may be deductible only if they can be directly traced to the Korean business and supported by allocation methodology. Entertainment expenses are limited to 70% (SMEs) or 20% (large companies) of the amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Derived as Box 1 - Box 2 - Box 3. If negative, carry forward operating loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident corporations with a PE, operating income must reflect only activities attributable to the Korean PE. intercompany loans' interest may be imputed if debts exceed equity of 3:1 (thin capitalization).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, dividends received, FX gains/losses, donations, casualty losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends from foreign subsidiaries may be 100% exempt or subject to indirect foreign tax credit eligibility if active business. Interest expense on excessive offshore borrowings may be denied under thin capitalization rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 4 + Box 5 net result. Usually reported in financial statements adjusted for IFRS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile GAAP net income to tax basis. Non-deductible items, such as penalties, are added back. Foreign exchange differences should be tax-recognised in accordance with accrual principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary differences: non-taxable receipts, non-deductible expenses, depreciation recapture, and deferred tax assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Depreciation cannot exceed Korea MACRS-style rates. Provisions and reserves are generally not deductible except as permitted. For foreign corporations, the head office's expenses allocated to the Korean branch must be substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 6 +/− Box 7 adjustments, reduced by available loss carryforwards (up to 10 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards are available only if a tax return was filed in the loss year; a change of 50% or more in shareholders may trigger a loss disallowance. Foreign corporations may not use losses of foreign PE against Korean income unless treaty allows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply progressive corporate income tax rates to taxable income in Box 8.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the rate schedule: 10%, 20%, 22%, 25% as applicable. For non-residents without a PE, no CIT return is due on Korean-source dividends if WHT is applied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D credits, foreign tax credits, investment tax credits, and treaty-based exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits must be documented with tax invoices. Treaty exemptions require submission of a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership certificates. Carryforward of unused FTC is 10 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Total Tax Payable After Credits (차감납부세액)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 9 - Box 10, plus any additional surtax (local income tax at 10% of CIT).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Local income tax (지방소득세) is 10% of corporate tax due. File via separate local tax portal (Wetax, wetax.go.kr). For foreign taxpayers, include the local surtax in the consolidated declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Semi-annual preliminary payments, amounts withheld by joint venture partners, and other prior year payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report preliminary payments made in August and October. Non-resident entities with interest revenue subject to WHT may credit the withholding as advance payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 13 - Final Amount Due or Refund (차감세액·환숙세액)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 11 - Box 12. If positive, pay by the filing deadline; if negative, claim refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refunds to foreign entities generally processed within 30 days; but Korean NTS may trigger a special audit for non-residents. Ensure all supporting documents are in Korean or translated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of the unpaid tax if filed within one month after deadline; additional of 0.75% per month, up to 36 months. Understated tax penalty: 10% of understated amount (or up to 40% for intentional concealment). Failure to pay: 0.825% per month surcharge. Criminal penalties for fraudulent returns: imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to 5 times the evaded tax under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge) on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced by a tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply for a reduced rate: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority (OECD-standard format) issued within the same year; (2) complete and submit the 'Application for Abatement of Tax with Respect to a Tax Treaty' (Form IR 20) to the Korean withholding agent before payment; (3) provide a beneficial ownership certificate and supporting documents proving active trader status (not a conduit); (4) submit the required declaration through HomeTax or to a local tax office; (5) the foreign recipient must inform the Korean payer of any changes in residence. If approval is not obtained before payment, the payer must withhold at the statutory rate and the recipient may file for a refund within 5 years, attaching full documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 22% aggregate; treaty rates often reduced to 10% (e.g., US-Korea, Japan-Korea treaties) or 5% for financial institutions. Royalties: statutory 22%; treaty rates typically 10% for industrial/computer software royalties, sometimes 5% for cultural royalties. Must prove beneficial ownership and deductibility of royalty (expense) is only allowed if not excessive.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Korean Won (KRW): Local File must be prepared when total cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.4M); Master File required when such transactions exceed KRW 50 billion (approx. USD 37M); Country-by-Country Report required when combined group revenue is at least KRW 1 trillion (approx. USD 740M). Documentation must be submitted within 30 days of an official request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Korea does not apply offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), the substance-over-form doctrine and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) in the Framework Act for National Taxes (FANT) permit the NTS to recharacterise transactions lacking economic substance. A Korean company must have a fixed place of business, active management, sufficient employees, and undertake Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Korea to satisfy the permanent establishment threshold and to claim treaty benefits. Failure to demonstrate substance can lead to denial of treaty benefits and the imputation of income to the controlling foreign parent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directing employees to under-report wholesale turnover of SSD/CPU chips, creating fake invoices or using informal payments to conceal profits; failure to file a tax return for three consecutive years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 9(1) of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, evasion of corporate income tax is punishable by imprisonment of up to two years or a fine not exceeding twice the amount evaded. Additionally, the National Tax Basic Act imposes an unpaid tax surcharge of 3% per annum (up to 27 months) and a negligence penalty of 20%–40% of the understated tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participated in the evasion may be held personally liable for the corporate tax debt (joint and several), under Art. 16(1) of the Corporate Tax Act, if they consumed or concealed corporate assets. Criminal prosecution can lead to travel bans (blacklisted by the NTS), asset freezing, and imprisonment up to 2 years. Offshore accounts must be disclosed under the Foreign Exchange Act, failure to do so adds 1 year imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payments of royalties for semiconductor IP or software to a non-resident licensor, or dividends to a non-resident parent, without withholding the mandatory 22% (or treaty-reduced rate) and remitting to the NTS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 98 of the Corporate Income Tax Act, the payer becomes liable for the un-withheld tax plus a 10% negligence penalty (or 20% in cases of deliberate non-withholding), and daily surcharges of 0.0225%. Additionally, Article 16 of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act imposes a fine of up to KRW 30 million or imprisonment up to 2 years for willful failure to withhold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign off on payments without a valid treaty relief application are personally responsible for the withheld amount; the NTS may issue a personal collection notice and a ban on travel (blacklisting). If the director uses cross-border accounts to disguise payments, money-laundering charges under the Specific Financial Information Act may attach, leading to asset confiscation and up to 5 years imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Thin Capitalisation Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling SSD and CPU chips to a related distributor at artificially low prices to shift profits abroad, or borrowing excessively from a foreign parent (debt-to-equity ratio exceeding 3:1) with excessive interest rates, while failing to prepare transfer pricing files despite exceeding the KRW 10 billion threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 10 of the International Tax Adjustment Act (ITA Act), the tax authority may recompute taxable income at arm's-length and impose an additional tax of up to 30% of the understated taxable income. Failure to produce TP reports upon request results in a civil penalty of up to KRW 100 million and denial of offsetting adjustments for the foreign counterparty. Thin capitalisation interest disallowance is 30% of the excess interest paid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The 'supervising director' may be personally fined up to KRW 10 million for gross negligence in maintaining adequate TP documentation. Criminal charges may be filed if the manipulation is intentional, with imprisonment up to 2 years. In severe cases, the NTS can seek a court order to freeze personal assets of the directors and revoke the corporate business licence.
